identity.name: Cosmograph Daytona
identity.one_liner: The 1988-2000 automatic Daytona built on a reworked Zenith El Primero — the reference that started the Daytona waitlist.

comps.condition: Circa 1998, Switzerland; Stainless steel; Accompanied by a Rolex warranty, green leather Rolex presentation box, leather wallet, numbered hang tag and chronometer hang tag, wax seal, product literature, and outer packaging; Factory-stickered new-old-stock, unworn, complete-set example; condition premium makes it non-comparable to an ordinary 16520.

narrative.story: Rolex's first self-winding Daytona used the Zenith El Primero as its base, slowed from 36,000 to 28,800 vph and reworked so heavily that roughly half the parts changed. The 40mm case, sapphire crystal, and glossy dials set the Daytona's modern shape, and demand outran supply almost immediately — the Daytona waitlist is a 16520-era invention. Collectors track it by dial marks, from early 'floating' Cosmograph text to inverted-6 subdials.
narrative.collector_notes: 'Patrizzi' dials — subdial rings oxidized to brown on circa 1994-95 examples — carry a premium, as do early floating-dial and four-line versions. Service dials and replacement hands are common; period-correct parts drive the price.
